sections.heading: Overall Engagement Performance
sections.body: The 2025 engagement survey achieved a response rate of 87%, representing 3,842 employees across all regions. Our overall engagement score increased to 78%, up 6 percentage points from 72% in 2024, marking the strongest year-on-year improvement since 2021. Notable gains were observed in “Pride in the Organisation” (+9 points) and “Confidence in Senior Leadership” (+7 points). Despite this progress, variability between functions and demographic groups indicates that further targeted action is required.

sections.heading: Key Driver Analysis
sections.body: Regression analysis identified three primary engagement drivers for 2025: Manager Effectiveness, Career Development Opportunities, and Workload Sustainability. Manager Effectiveness showed the strongest correlation with engagement (r=0.64) and improved by 5 points year-on-year. However, Career Development scored 68%, remaining 10 points below the overall engagement average, particularly among early-career professionals. Workload Sustainability improved marginally (+2 points), but qualitative comments highlight continued pressure in client-facing teams.

sections.heading: Demographic and Segment Insights
sections.body: Engagement among employees with less than two years’ tenure stands at 70%, compared to 82% for those with over five years’ service. Women reported an engagement score of 75%, five points below men at 80%, with the largest gap appearing in perceptions of advancement fairness. Regionally, the Northern Operations division scored 83%, while Central Services lagged at 71%, largely due to concerns around role clarity and workload distribution. These measurable gaps provide a clear basis for targeted intervention.

sections.heading: Year-on-Year Trends
sections.body: Since 2023, overall engagement has risen from 69% to 78%, reflecting sustained improvement across most survey dimensions. Trust in immediate managers has improved consistently (+4 points in 2024, +5 points in 2025), aligning with our investment in leadership capability programmes. Conversely, perceptions of cross-functional collaboration have plateaued at 73% for two consecutive years. Exit interview data corroborates survey findings, particularly regarding career progression transparency.

sections.heading: Prioritised People Action Plan (2026)
sections.body: The Executive Committee has endorsed a 12-month action plan focused on three priorities: (1) Launching structured career pathways and internal mobility dashboards by Q3 2026; (2) Expanding manager coaching accreditation to 100% of people leaders by year-end; and (3) Implementing workload planning pilots in Central Services and Client Delivery teams by Q2. Success metrics include a minimum 4-point increase in Career Development scores and a 50% reduction in the gender engagement gap by the 2026 survey cycle. Quarterly pulse surveys will track progress and ensure accountability at divisional level.

2025 Employee Engagement Survey – Results Overview and Action Priorities
Ref: HR-ENG-25-17 | Date: 18 February 2026 | From: Priya Deshmukh, Chief People Officer

Section Overall Engagement Performance
The 2025 engagement survey achieved a response rate of 87%, representing 3,842 employees across all regions. Our overall engagement score increased to 78%, up 6 percentage points from 72% in 2024, marking the strongest year-on-year improvement since 2021. Notable gains were observed in “Pride in the Organisation” (+9 points) and “Confidence in Senior Leadership” (+7 points). Despite this progress, variability between functions and demographic groups indicates that further targeted action is required.

Section Key Driver Analysis
Regression analysis identified three primary engagement drivers for 2025: Manager Effectiveness, Career Development Opportunities, and Workload Sustainability. Manager Effectiveness showed the strongest correlation with engagement (r=0.64) and improved by 5 points year-on-year. However, Career Development scored 68%, remaining 10 points below the overall engagement average, particularly among early-career professionals. Workload Sustainability improved marginally (+2 points), but qualitative comments highlight continued pressure in client-facing teams.

Section Demographic and Segment Insights
Engagement among employees with less than two years’ tenure stands at 70%, compared to 82% for those with over five years’ service. Women reported an engagement score of 75%, five points below men at 80%, with the largest gap appearing in perceptions of advancement fairness. Regionally, the Northern Operations division scored 83%, while Central Services lagged at 71%, largely due to concerns around role clarity and workload distribution. These measurable gaps provide a clear basis for targeted intervention.

Section Year-on-Year Trends
Since 2023, overall engagement has risen from 69% to 78%, reflecting sustained improvement across most survey dimensions. Trust in immediate managers has improved consistently (+4 points in 2024, +5 points in 2025), aligning with our investment in leadership capability programmes. Conversely, perceptions of cross-functional collaboration have plateaued at 73% for two consecutive years. Exit interview data corroborates survey findings, particularly regarding career progression transparency.

Section Prioritised People Action Plan (2026)
The Executive Committee has endorsed a 12-month action plan focused on three priorities: (1) Launching structured career pathways and internal mobility dashboards by Q3 2026; (2) Expanding manager coaching accreditation to 100% of people leaders by year-end; and (3) Implementing workload planning pilots in Central Services and Client Delivery teams by Q2. Success metrics include a minimum 4-point increase in Career Development scores and a 50% reduction in the gender engagement gap by the 2026 survey cycle. Quarterly pulse surveys will track progress and ensure accountability at divisional level.

text_content: **Key Driver Insights, Demographic Breakdowns, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan**

The survey’s key driver analysis identifies three primary predictors of engagement: Manager Support (r=0.62), Career Growth (r=0.58), and Recognition (r=0.55). These correlations indicate moderate to strong relationships with overall engagement and guide priority focus areas for line leaders and People & Culture. Manager Support’s r=0.62 suggests that improvements in supervisory practices will yield the largest incremental gains, while Career Growth and Recognition present meaningful secondary leverage. The analysis also highlights interaction effects between Manager Support and Recognition, suggesting combined interventions may produce greater uplift over time.

100 for employees with tenure 5+ years, indicating a 12-point decline associated with longer tenure. Additional segmentation shows frontline operations scoring 4 percentage points below corporate functions, and Region East outperforming Region West by 6 percentage points. Gender and age cohorts show smaller differentials (<3 points) after statistical adjustment. These patterns inform targeted retention and career-pathing interventions for high-tenure groups during the next quarter.

The prioritised 90-day People action plan assigns three enterprise-level initiatives to People & Culture with clear deliverables, metrics, and deadlines: 1. Launch Manager Coaching Program (due 30 June 2025) to address Manager Support; 2. Publish a Career Pathways Framework (due 31 July 2025) to strengthen Career Growth; 3. Implement a Recognition Platform and quarterly awards (due 31 August 2025) to improve Recognition. People & Culture will report progress weekly to Executive Sponsor, track engagement delta by cohort, and measure success using target increases in driver sub-scores.
